guide.title: Stowe Mountain Resort, Vermont: Mount Mansfield, from rope tow to Vail Resorts
guide.intro: Lift-served skiing at Stowe began on February 7, 1937, when Craig Burt, the Mt. Mansfield Ski Club, and Sepp Ruschp opened a rope tow on the Toll House slope of Mount Mansfield, per New England Ski History's "Stowe" area history page. On November 17, 1940, Mt. Mansfield Lift, Inc. -- led by Sepp Ruschp, Lowell Thomas, and Roland Palmedo -- opened a single chairlift billed at the time as the longest and highest chairlift in the world, at 6,330 feet in length and 2,030 feet of vertical rise; despite breaking down on opening day, it remained in service for nearly 50 years. Mount Mansfield is also where Charles Minot Dole, leader of the Mt. Mansfield Ski Patrol, founded the National Ski Patrol in 1938 after ski-accident experiences on the mountain, according to Wikipedia's "National Ski Patrol" article.

sections.heading: AIG ownership, then Vail Resorts
sections.body: AIG founder C.V. Starr began financing the ski area around 1946 and by 1950 had consolidated five separate operating companies into the Mount Mansfield Company, establishing majority ownership that continued under AIG-affiliated control for decades, per New England Ski History's "Stowe" area history page. Vail Resorts' acquisition of Stowe -- its first resort on the East Coast of the United States -- is dated to February 21, 2017 in Vail Resorts' own corporate resort listing, per Wikipedia's "Vail Resorts" article. New England Ski History states the Stowe sale to Vail Resorts closed in June 2017 for a reported $41 million, ending roughly 70 years of AIG-affiliated ownership dating back to C.V. Starr. The Sunrise Six detachable chairlift replaced the older Mountain Triple chairlift in the 2022-23 season, per Wikipedia's "Stowe Mountain Resort" article.

sections.heading: Billy Kidd, from Stowe to Innsbruck
sections.body: Billy Kidd grew up in Stowe and raced with the Mount Mansfield Ski Team before becoming, with teammate Jimmie Heuga, the first American men to win an Olympic alpine skiing medal, taking silver in slalom at the 1964 Innsbruck Games at age 20, according to Wikipedia's "Billy Kidd" article.

sections.heading: In Stowe
sections.body: Maria and Georg von Trapp, who fled Austria after its 1938 annexation by Nazi Germany, settled in Stowe in 1942 and in 1950 began operating their home as a commercial ski lodge, the origin of today's Trapp Family Lodge, per Wikipedia's "Trapp Family Lodge" article. The original lodge burned down on December 20, 1980, and was replaced by a new Austrian-style lodge that opened in December 1983; the property remains family-owned and was rebranded "von Trapp Family Lodge & Resort" in February 2025. The Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum was established in 1988 in Brandon, Vermont, relocated to Stowe in 2000, and reopened at its current Main Street location -- a building originally constructed in 1818 as the town's Old Town Hall -- after a 2002 renovation; "Snowboard" was added to the museum's name in 2011. Green Mountain Inn was built in 1833 by Peter C. Lovejoy and took its current name in 1893; it is a contributing property to the Stowe Village Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places on November 15, 1978, per Wikipedia's "Green Mountain Inn" article. The Alchemist was founded in 2003 by John and Jen Kimmich as a brewpub in Waterbury, Vermont, known for its Heady Topper IPA; Tropical Storm Irene flooded the Waterbury pub in 2011, and the brewery opened a second, visitor-accessible brewery and cafe at 100 Cottage Club Road in Stowe in 2016, per The Alchemist's own "Story" page. The Current, an art center and library, is housed in an 1863 Greek Revival building originally built as the Stowe Village School; it opened there in 1981, funded by a bequest from the late Helen Day Montanari, and rebranded itself as "The Current" in 2021, per Wikipedia's "Helen Day Memorial Library and Art Center" article. Gold Brook Covered Bridge, south of Stowe village, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Smugglers' Notch State Park's official address, according to Vermont State Parks' own page, is 6443 Mountain Road in Stowe, placing the park's office and campground roughly 6.5 miles northwest of Stowe village on VT Route 108 near Mount Mansfield.

faq.question: Who owns Stowe Mountain Resort?
faq.answer: Vail Resorts has owned Stowe since a sale that closed in June 2017 for a reported $41 million, ending roughly 70 years of AIG-affiliated ownership dating back to founder C.V. Starr, per New England Ski History's "Stowe" area history page. It was Vail's first resort on the East Coast.

faq.question: What ski history connects to Stowe besides the resort itself?
faq.answer: Charles Minot Dole founded the National Ski Patrol in 1938 after ski-accident experiences on Mount Mansfield, per Wikipedia's "National Ski Patrol" article, and Billy Kidd raced with the Mount Mansfield Ski Team before winning Olympic silver in slalom at the 1964 Innsbruck Games.

places.name: Trapp Family Lodge
places.summary: A family-owned mountain lodge founded by Maria and Georg von Trapp after they settled in Stowe in 1942.
places.history: Maria and Georg von Trapp, who fled Austria after its 1938 annexation by Nazi Germany, settled in Stowe in 1942 and in 1950 began operating their home as a commercial ski lodge, the origin of today's Trapp Family Lodge, per Wikipedia's "Trapp Family Lodge" article. The original lodge burned down on December 20, 1980, and was replaced by a new Austrian-style lodge that opened in December 1983; the property remains family-owned and was rebranded "von Trapp Family Lodge & Resort" in February 2025.

places.name: Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum
places.summary: A ski and snowboard history museum in Stowe's former Old Town Hall.
places.history: The museum was established in 1988 in Brandon, Vermont as The Vermont Ski Museum, relocated to Stowe in 2000, and reopened at its current Main Street location -- a building originally constructed in 1818 as the town's Old Town Hall -- after a 2002 renovation, per Wikipedia's "Vermont Ski and Snowboard Museum" article. "Snowboard" was added to the museum's name in 2011 to reflect an expanded collection, including equipment, clothing, and fine art, plus a permanent Hall of Fame exhibit.

places.name: Green Mountain Inn
places.summary: An 1833 inn on Main Street, a contributing property of the Stowe Village Historic District.
places.history: Green Mountain Inn was built in 1833 by Peter C. Lovejoy and was successively known as the Mansfield House and the Brick Hotel before taking its current name in 1893 when purchased by Mark C. Lovejoy, per Wikipedia's "Green Mountain Inn" article. The inn is a contributing property to the Stowe Village Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places on November 15, 1978 (ID 78000236), and has been owned by the Gameroff Trust since Marvin Gameroff's 1982 purchase.

places.name: The Alchemist
places.summary: A brewery known for its Heady Topper IPA, with a visitor brewery and cafe in Stowe since 2016.
places.history: The Alchemist was founded in 2003 by John and Jen Kimmich as a brewpub in Waterbury, Vermont, known for its Heady Topper IPA, per The Alchemist's own "Story" page. Tropical Storm Irene flooded the Waterbury pub in 2011. The Alchemist opened a second, visitor-accessible brewery and cafe at 100 Cottage Club Road in Stowe in 2016, alongside its production facility, which remained in Waterbury.

places.name: The Current
places.summary: An art center and library in Stowe's former 1863 village school, rebranded "The Current" in 2021.
places.history: This art center and library is housed in an 1863 Greek Revival building originally built as the Stowe Village School; the art center and library opened there in 1981, funded by a bequest from the late Helen Day Montanari, and the art center rebranded itself as "The Current" in 2021, per Wikipedia's "Helen Day Memorial Library and Art Center" article.

places.name: Gold Brook Covered Bridge
places.summary: A covered bridge south of Stowe village, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
places.history: Gold Brook Covered Bridge, south of Stowe village, is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, per Wikipedia's list of National Register of Historic Places listings in Lamoille County, Vermont.

places.name: Smugglers' Notch State Park
places.summary: A state park office and campground on the Stowe side of Smugglers' Notch, near Mount Mansfield.
places.history: Smugglers' Notch State Park's official address, according to Vermont State Parks' own page, is 6443 Mountain Road in Stowe -- placing the park's office and campground on the Stowe side of the notch, roughly 6.5 miles northwest of Stowe village on VT Route 108 near Mount Mansfield.
